text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"security_deposits","status":"in_force","title":"California residential security deposit cap, return deadline and itemization rules","requirement":"A landlord may not demand or receive security (any payment, fee, deposit or charge imposed at the beginning of the tenancy, including charges to reimburse costs of processing a new tenant or advance payments of rent) exceeding one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Small landlords (natural persons or LLCs whose members are all natural persons, owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units total) may not demand or receive more than two months' rent, except that this higher cap does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer. For service members charged a higher than standard security due to credit or housing history, a written explanation is required and the additional amount must be returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears. Security may not be characterized as nonrefundable. Landlord must offer an initial inspection and give an itemized statement of deductions; must take photographs at move-in (tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01) and at move-out. Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement with supporting documents and return the remaining security (electronically if rent or deposit was received electronically). Deductions of $125 or less in total need not be documented.
